Q: Permute rows and columns to put largest values as close to diagonal as possible A:

I think this may be close to what you want.

Up front, this answer is "inefficient" in the sense of memory management, since every pass through the loop makes a full copy of the frame. This is largely unavoidable unless we use data.table or similar for referential semantics. For frames that are under 100 rows (as I believe yours are) this is largely a theoretical problem and unlikely to pose any problem. (There is certainly a better way to do this.)

For each column:

  • omit rows locked in in the previous columns (stored in row_used)
  • assuming < 0.01 is uninteresting (effectively 0), find the order of the values
  • sort the frame such that the previously locked in rows are first, then the remaining rows are ordered by their decreasing values
data3 <- data1 # copy to preserve for demonstration
row_used <- 0L
for (cn in 1:ncol(data3)) {
  vals <- if (cn == 1L) data3[[cn]] else data3[[cn]][-(1:row_used)]
  ord <- c(seq_len(row_used), row_used + order(-vals))
  data3 <- data3[ord,]
  row_used <- row_used + sum(vals >= 0.01)
}

I'll use tibble::as_tibble here solely because it makes a much easier distinction between zero and non-zero values, it has nothing to do with the implementation. It does remove the row names from its display. This too can be mitigated if you wanted to shift to tibbles (for instance, bring the row names in as a column, which your previous larger data has).

as_tibble(data3)

Q: SwiftUI: Showing white sheet for first time A:

Very common problem it's because the sheet is only dependent on the show sheet bool not the document. To fix you can either change to use the sheet(item:) api

.sheet(item: $documentURL) { doc in

or do this

.sheet(isPresented: $showShareSheet) { [documentURL] in

Another way is to put the bool and document in the same state struct which is what we did before sheet(item:) was added to SwiftUI and still required today if you want the sheet to be able to change the document.

The downside to sheet(item:) is if the document is changed then the sheet will dismiss and present again which looks a kinda bad.

Q: The auto-completion for await changes the method's signature - how do I prevent that? A:

Q: Godot shader not detecting pixel colour A:

Q: namespaces in headers(compiler-explorer) A:

Explanation of the error message

Apparently your source code has an #include that makes the preprocessor expect the file "index_kdtree.h" in the folder "efanna2e", but it is not there.

Conclusion

Unfortunately you do not provide a minimal reproducible example. Therefore the only thing to say is: Correct your #include or the header file's location.

Q: How to send a custom variable in a flask in Flask to JS/HTML to render an image? A:
  1. Sanitize the file name
  2. Concatenate your variable inside the string for the Jinja2 variable
account_name = secure_filename(account_name)
<img src="{{url_for('static', filename='#UserData/' ~ account_name ~ '/profile/profile_pic.jpg')}"  width='200' height='200' />

(Also, are you sure that you want that hashtag before UserData, and that mix of camel case and snake case? Better to use dash case for HTML. )
